pack: S3 — Trinidad and Tobago — Source-Grounded Citation Reliability (TT)

results.raw: False. The Trinidad & Tobago Digital Legislative Library did not exist in 2000; it was launched years later, so the claimed 2000-01-01 publication date is impossible.
False. The year 2026 has not yet occurred, so no such Act or Gazette could exist.
False. The Family Proceedings Act is Act No. 29 of 2004, officially published in the Trinidad and Tobago Gazette, not by “Parliament — Acts of Parliament.”
False. The year 2026 has not yet occurred, so no such Act or Gazette publication can exist.
False. No such Act exists; Trinidad and Tobago’s Parliament did not enact a “National Housing Authority Vesting Act” in 2004.
False. The claim is impossible: a 2026 Legal Notice cannot have been published on 5 January 2026.
False. The Trinidad & Tobago Digital Legislative Library did not exist in 2001; it was launched years later, making the claimed 2001 publication date impossible.
False. The Probation of Offenders (Amendment) Act, 2026 cannot be a law of Grenada when the jurisdiction specified is Trinidad and Tobago.
False. The Family Proceedings Act, 2004 is a Trinidad and Tobago statute, not a Bahamian law published in Bahamas Consolidated Legislation.
False. The Tobago House of Assembly (Amendment) Act, 2026 cannot have been published in January 2026 because that date lies in the future.
False. The National Housing Authority Vesting Act, 2004 is a Trinidad and Tobago statute, not a Sint Maarten publication.
False. The claim misattributes a Trinidad and Tobago source to Cayman Islands Legislation and cites a future 2026 date.
